answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable stake before it can trade. A fake account is cheap to forge, but every fake one has to lock real money that gets slashed when it misbehaves. A good anchor is a record of past work tied to that stake, so a new identity starts with no trust and has to earn it slowly. An attacker facing a karst of thin, separate accounts finds each one costs money and time to build up, while one honest identity with a solid history keeps its deposit and its reputation.
